addresses: MAJOR, visual-desktop: "'Planning Center holds no other record of her' is a claim about the whole upstream directory; what Tally actually checked is one id (410/404) and one merge trail … Priya, reading a sentence that tells her a second copy is impossible, presses the one loud button and writes the duplicate."
visual-desktop: 'the identical promise is earned there and unearned here' — the visitor path in sync-blocked matches before it creates; the linked path does not.

design-desktop: 'a 168-character guarantee sentence sitting inside the action column … move it into the message column where the rest of the narration already lives, and leave beside the button only the short guard the family's own rule allows.'
changes.change: The guarantee stopped asserting the absence of a record nobody searched for, and moved out of the action column into the message column where the rest of the narration lives. The strip's body now ends: '…deleted outright, not merged into anybody. Nothing is lost: the correction is still held here, and so is every gathering she attended — re-creating sends it with her, so nobody types it twice. Tally searches Planning Center for a matching person first and links to her if it finds one, rather than adding a second.' Beside the button there is now only a 35-character guard, and it is deliberately sync-blocked's words verbatim: 'One new person, never a second copy.' The primary and the guard are bound together in one wrapper (gap-1) with the retreat pushed off below it. The strip is the same height it was; four lines of fine print became three lines of narration.
changes.rationale: Two sentences were available — shrink the claim to what was checked, or make the claim true — and the second is the one that leaves the product better, because the promise is the reason the button is safe to press. So the copy now describes a behaviour rather than a state of the world: 'searches first and links if it finds one' is true of the fixed path and says nothing about the directory Tally has not read. The office admin who cleaned up a duplicate by hand is exactly the reader this sentence is now written for — it tells her what happens in her case instead of denying her case exists. Keeping the short guard in sync-blocked's exact words is the point of doing the code change: once both re-creates go through the same match-then-create, the same promise is earned in the same words on both frames, and a reader who has seen one recognises the other.
changes.breakpoint: both — it is copy and one wrapper element, identical at 390px and 1440px
changes.implementation: Two halves, and the code half is the load-bearing one. (1) `functions/src/pco/recreate.ts`: the linked (`pco_…`) branch must stop being a bare `client.post('/people', …)` — the create at line 180 — and go through the same match-then-create the visitor push already uses. Before creating, call `findExistingPeople(client, config, firstName, lastName, grade ?? null)` and `pickExistingPerson(...)` from `./pushStudents.js` (both already exported; the visitor branch reaches them through `pushStudent`). If a person comes back, link to it with the membership migration this function already performs for a created id — the `pcoStudentId(personId)` document, `recreatedFromStudentId`/`recreatedAsStudentId` pointers, `upstreamRecordMissing: false` — and return `status: 'relinked'` with a message that says a matching record was found rather than created. Only an empty match list reaches `client.post('/people', …)`. The match is the strict one (first name, last name and grade, re-filtered locally through `nameGradeKey`, `child: true` required when the grade is blank), so it cannot graft a child onto a same-named adult volunteer. Update the file header comment: the matching path is no longer 'for a visitor document … on purpose', it is both branches. (2) `StudentSyncStrip`, `state='orphaned'`: the guarantee prose joins the `body` string; the actions column's caption becomes the constant `'One new person, never a second copy.'`, the same string `SyncNotice` renders on the blocked-create notice — pull it out to one shared constant so the two frames cannot drift apart.

addresses: MINOR, design-phone: 'a value that appears in a cell does not appear in the paragraph. Both people and the date are stated in prose first and then again as the comparison, so the two-up arrives as a recap.'
MINOR, design-desktop: 'the survivor's name is set five times and the day four … the reader is being told the same two facts in four registers.'
design-phone: 'If the ids are what carry the distinction, they should not be the quietest thing in the cell that holds them.'
changes.change: The cells took the two people and the date; the paragraph kept only what the cells cannot say. It went from 'Planning Center merged Ava Chen into Ava Chen-Ito on Tuesday. Your correction followed the merge and landed on her, not here — she already held that surname, so nothing changed. This page now reads from her.' to 'Your correction followed the merge and landed on the survivor, not here — she already held that surname, so no value changed. This page now reads from her, and the ids below are what moved.' No name and no date is now set twice. In the cells the ids stopped being the quietest text in the object that carries the state: `#AC377` and `#AC101` are `font-semibold tabular-nums text-ink-100` and the words around them lifted from `ink-500` to `ink-400`, so the line reads id-first. The paragraph lost two lines and the strip is 40px shorter at 1440px.
changes.rationale: This is the rule the family adopted for `differs` last round applied to the frame that was cut from it, so it is a correction rather than a new decision. The last clause is the one piece of new writing and it earns its place: it is the only sentence that tells a reader why two cells holding almost the same name are worth reading, which is exactly the silent case this scene exists to render. Lifting the ids rather than demoting the names was the cheaper half — once the paragraph no longer gives the names away, the name is a legitimate figure again, and only the provenance line needed rank.
changes.breakpoint: both — copy plus two ink-ramp steps, the same at both widths
changes.implementation: `StudentSyncStrip`, `state='merged'`: the body string takes no `survivor.name`, no `named.name` and no `mergedAt`; those three go to the `<dl>` only. This is the same rule round 3 wrote for `differs` and it is now the family's: a value, a name or a timestamp that appears in a cell does not appear in the paragraph. In the cell's second `<dd>`, the id gets `font-semibold tabular-nums text-ink-100` and the surrounding provenance words `text-ink-400`, applied wherever the cell's distinguishing fact is the id rather than the figure.

addresses: MINOR, visual-phone: 'once the strip is dismissed the only carrier is a `title` a thumb cannot open, and the real-text version is a screen and a half down … Either the chip scrolls to the provenance line when tapped, or Got it collapses the strip to one line.'
MINOR, design-desktop: 'the provenance line overruns its measure and splits the one action phrase in the card, leaving a single orphaned word underlined on its own line.'
changes.change: The chip is now the way into its own explanation. `≠ Merged upstream · Tue` is an `<a href="#pc-provenance">` carrying a trailing `↓`, and the Profile card's Planning Center block is the target — so the sentence a pointer gets on hover is the sentence a thumb gets on tap, in real text, without hunting. The chip's ink, size and dashed ring are unchanged; the hit area alone grows, to 44px tall under a thumb, through a pseudo-element that leaves the visual box exactly where it was and collapses back to the ink at lg. The provenance line itself was shortened to 'Read from **Ava Chen-Ito** since Tuesday's merge.' — the section heading already says Planning Center — so 'Open their profile' now sits whole on one line at both widths instead of stranding 'profile'.
changes.rationale: This is the critic's own first option, and it is the one that survives a real render: collapsing the strip to a one-line summary on 'Got it' needs two states of one frame, and the state that would prove it is the state nobody can see. Anchoring costs one attribute and one id and leaves the fact where it already was, in the card whose job is provenance. Growing only the hit area is the reading of 'do not make the chip bigger' that keeps both goals: nothing on the glass changes, and a thumb still gets a 44px target for the one tap this chip ever takes. The `↓` is a single character, which is the app's whole icon language, and it is the only thing that says the chip goes somewhere.
changes.breakpoint: both in markup; the hit-area growth is below lg only — at lg and up the pointer hovers the tooltip and the pseudo-element shrinks to the chip
changes.implementation: `JobChip` takes an optional `href` and renders an `<a>` instead of a `<span>` when it has one, with `relative cursor-pointer after:absolute after:-inset-y-3 after:-inset-x-1 after:content-[''] lg:after:inset-0`. `StudentIdentityHeader` passes `href='#planning-center'` for `merged` and for no other state — a chip is only ever a link when the page holds the same fact in prose. The Profile card's Planning Center block gets `id="planning-center"` and `scroll-mt-4`. The provenance string drops the redundant 'in Planning Center'; it reads `Read from {survivor.name} since {mergedAt} merge.` with the link after it.

addresses: MINOR, visual-desktop: 'Every other job state in this journey has a row form on sync-students … merged has none, so the one state in the dangerous class is the one J2 cannot see coming. Give merged its own word in the chip, not differs' — ≠ Merged upstream with the survivor named in the tooltip — and decide once whether such a row counts in Needs you (it should).'
MINOR, visual-phone: 'Share the mark, not the word: ≠ Merged on the row, ≠ Changed for the upstream value conflict.'
changes.change: One merged row, on Noah O'Brien-Hale. The row's name is the survivor's, which is the fact the state turns on — a leader mid-run scanning for the surname she typed sees one she did not. The chip is `≠ Merged upstream · Tue` at lg and `≠ Merged` below it, in the same danger tone and the same `≠` the family already uses for differs; the desktop caption follows the family's `{what} · {who}` pattern with 'Was Noah O'Brien · you', and the tooltip names the survivor and says why nothing here will resolve it. `Needs you` went 2 → 3. Petra Raman's row is untouched: '≠ Changed upstream · 2m' / '≠ Changed' still means somebody changed a field, and now the two errands are one glance apart.
changes.rationale: The word is the whole finding. 'Changed' and 'Merged' are the same shape of trouble and completely different errands — one is a two-value choice, the other is 'this child is now a different Planning Center person, go look' — and on a phone the word is all a row gets, because the caption is `hidden lg:`. Sharing the mark keeps the glyph family closed, which round 3 declined to reopen and which nothing here needs. Counting it in `Needs you` follows the count's own rule rather than the state's severity: `In flight` is what will finish on its own, `Needs you` is what will not, and a merge never resolves itself. Putting the survivor's surname on the row rather than the one that was typed is the honest render — it is what the list will actually show after `readThroughMerges` follows the trail, and a frame that showed the old name would hide the surprise the state exists to give.
changes.breakpoint: both — one row, one chip, one count; the short word below lg and the long word plus caption at lg, exactly as every other state on this list
changes.implementation: `JobChip`'s word map gains `merged: { long: 'Merged upstream', short: 'Merged' }` — the glyph map is still untouched, `merged` keeps `differs`' `≠` and `bad` tone. The `needsYou` count becomes `count(state in {differs, failed, orphaned, merged})`; `inFlight` is unchanged. The row caption for `merged` is `Was {named.name}` in the `{what}` slot with the queuing leader in the `{who}` slot, and the row renders under the survivor's name because that is what the student document resolves to after the graft — no special case in `StudentRow`, it simply reads the name it is given.

addresses: MINOR, design-phone: 'The action column is spaced as three equal steps, so the caption that qualifies the primary sits exactly as far from the button it explains as from the retreat it does not … sync-orphaned does it the other way. Two frames with the same anatomy resolve the same three parts differently.'
design-desktop: 'the caption sits above the primary here and below it on sync-merged — the same slot, opposite order. The guard belongs on one side of the primary across the whole family.'
changes.change: One order and one spacing, held across the strip family: the primary first, its caption bound to it, the retreat pushed off below. Structurally the primary and its caption are now one wrapper (`flex w-full flex-col gap-1 lg:w-auto`) inside a column that is `gap-4 lg:gap-2`, so caption-to-button is 4px and retreat-to-group is 16px under a thumb and 8px at a pointer. sync-orphaned's caption moved from above the button to below it; sync-merged's kept its place and gained the binding; sync-failed and sync-outage, which have a retreat and no caption, were rewritten from `gap-3` plus `mt-1 lg:mt-0` to the same `gap-4 lg:gap-2` — identical pixels, one rule instead of two spellings.
changes.rationale: The caption is a consequence of pressing the button, not a precondition for it — 'Opens her in Planning Center', 'One new person, never a second copy' — and a consequence reads after. Choosing merged's order over orphaned's also costs nothing: orphaned's caption was above only because it used to be a paragraph long, and it no longer is. Making the binding structural rather than a smaller gap value is what makes it survive: whatever the column's spacing becomes later, the caption cannot drift away from the button it belongs to, because it is inside it.
changes.breakpoint: both — the order and the wrapper are the same at both widths; only the gap between the group and the retreat is responsive, 16px below lg and 8px at lg and up, which is round 3's rule unchanged
changes.implementation: `StudentSyncStrip`'s actions column is one shape for every state: `<div class="flex flex-col gap-4 lg:gap-2 lg:max-w-80 lg:shrink-0">`, first child `<div class="flex w-full flex-col gap-1 lg:w-auto">` holding the primary and its optional caption, second child the retreat or the alternative action. No `mt-*` anywhere in this column. The r03 rule still stands on top of it: a caption in this column is under about 40 characters, and anything longer belongs in the message.

addresses: MINOR, design-desktop: 'the separator is the last mark on line one … hanging half a space off the end of a bold red phrase with nothing after it. It reads as a stray speck at the rag, or worse as a truncation mark.'
changes.change: Two moves. On every strip the separator is now bound to the body's first word with a non-breaking space, so it can never be the last mark on a line. And on the two scenes whose heading fills the measure — differs and merged — the run-in is dropped: heading and body stack at lg exactly as they already do below lg, and no separator is rendered at all, because there is nothing for it to separate. sync-failed, sync-profile, sync-orphaned and sync-outage keep the run-in, where the body genuinely continues on the heading's line and the middot sits mid-line doing its job.
changes.rationale: Binding alone was not enough and the render said so: with the mark glued to 'Your', the pair moved to line two together and the middot became a leading bullet — a different wrong mark in a different place. The critic's second option is the one that is actually true of these two frames, because a heading that fills the measure has already stopped running in; all that was left was to stop pretending. Doing both means the punctuation is right whichever way a heading falls, including headings nobody has written yet.
changes.breakpoint: lg and up — below lg the family already stacks and has never rendered the separator
changes.implementation: `StudentSyncStrip` renders the heading inline with the body only when the heading is short enough to leave room for the body's first words — a threshold of about 34 characters at the strip's lg measure; past that, heading and body are blocks and `separator` is not rendered. When it is rendered it is `{' \u00b7\u00a0'}` immediately followed by the body text, never `' \u00b7 '`, so the mark and the first word are one unbreakable unit.

declined.finding: MINOR, design-phone: 'Three buttons of the same rank, same fill and three different widths wrap into a right-aligned staircase … Either give them one common edge and one width, or collapse the two rarer ones behind the primary.'
declined.why: Declined, on the critic's own offer. This is the Students page header, it predates the sync work — the baseline already wrapped two of them — and nothing in this journey put the third button there. It is baseline furniture; taking it now would be relitigating the app rather than this journey, and the fix (a menu on the phone) is a change to a header that four other scenes share and that no round of this loop has looked at. It should be filed against the Students screen, not against profile-sync.

declined.finding: MINOR, design-desktop: 'the whole action stack has fallen onto a second row at the container's left edge, so a 1152px-wide strip carries all of its content in the left half … Do it and orphaned collapses back into the four-sibling silhouette with no other change.'
declined.why: Half done and half declined, and the measurement is why. Moving the guarantee out of the action column was right and is done — the column's 320px cap is gone and four lines of fine print with it. But the strip still wraps, and the caption was not what was causing it: the record page is `max-w-2xl`, so the strip's inner measure is 608px, and the message column's `lg:min-w-96` floor leaves 208px for the actions. 'Re-create her in Planning Center' is a 319px button on its own. To collapse the silhouette the label would have to lose 'in Planning Center' — on the one frame in the family where the button writes a new human into the church's permanent database, and where the label is the only thing on the button that says where. That is not a price worth paying for a family resemblance. The alternatives are worse in the ways round 3 already recorded: unpinning the message cap returns the strip to a 95-character measure, and wrapping the label to two lines makes the primary a paragraph. Recorded for the implementer: the rule is that an actions column wider than about 200px will wrap the strip at `max-w-2xl`, and that is a deliberate second row, not a bug — orphaned is the only state that reaches it.

declined.finding: The mark family (`‖` against `!`), the r01 scope declines (two-column record at lg, wider editor at lg), and the offline / `sending` / `waiting` frames.
declined.why: Not re-filed and not re-argued, per this round's instruction and last round's agreement. They stay declined, on the reasons already written down in the r02 and r03 records — including the one that matters for shipping: the offline branch of the queued strip is specified verbatim in r01 and r02 and the implementation must not ship the unconditional 'it goes on its own, even if you lock your phone' clause without it.
